identity.name: BoltWorks
identity.one_line_description: BoltWorks is a high-energy robotics learning club where young builders design, program, and compete with robots that bring big ideas to life.
identity.target_audience: Students aged 8–18, their parents, and educators looking for an after-school or weekend robotics program that blends STEM learning with competitive team spirit.

pages.title: Home
pages.goal: Immediately communicate the excitement and identity of BoltWorks, hook prospective students and parents, and guide them toward exploring the club or signing up.
pages.meta_description: BoltWorks is a festival-spirited robotics learning club for students who want to build, program, and compete. Discover our programs, teams, and upcoming events.

pages.title: About
pages.goal: Tell the BoltWorks origin story, introduce the club's values and leadership, and build trust with parents and prospective members through transparency and passion.
pages.meta_description: Learn about BoltWorks Robotics Club — our founding story, mission, values, and the passionate team that keeps the gears turning.

sections.intent: Set the editorial tone for the About page and frame the club's identity as a bold, community-driven movement.
sections.headline: Born in a Garage. Built for the World.
sections.subheadline: BoltWorks started with five kids, a pile of spare parts, and an unstoppable idea.
sections.body: What began as an informal weekend tinkering group in 2016 has grown into one of the region's most celebrated youth robotics clubs — a place where every student, regardless of background or experience, gets a seat at the build table.

asset_ideas.subject: A stylized vintage-poster illustration of a small garage workshop with oversized gears, tools, and a tiny robot on a workbench, evoking origin-story nostalgia
asset_ideas.purpose: Visual anchor for the founding narrative that reinforces the festival-poster aesthetic with a warm, celebratory tone

sections.intent: Deepen the origin narrative and articulate the mission and values that guide the club's culture and decisions.
sections.headline: We Build More Than Robots
sections.subheadline: Our mission is to spark a lifelong love of engineering in every student who walks through our doors.
sections.body: At BoltWorks, we believe the skills learned on the build floor — problem-solving, collaboration, resilience, and creative thinking — are the same skills that change the world. We don't just teach robotics. We build the next generation of engineers, innovators, and leaders.

items.title: Curiosity First
items.description: We celebrate questions over answers and reward experimentation, even when the robot falls over.

items.title: Every Builder Belongs
items.description: We actively recruit students from underrepresented communities and provide need-based scholarship access to all programs.

items.title: Real-World Rigor
items.description: Our curriculum is designed with input from working engineers to ensure students learn skills that matter beyond the competition floor.

items.title: Compete with Integrity
items.description: We train champions who win with grace, lose with dignity, and always help a rival team fix their robot before a match.

sections.intent: Introduce the leadership team and mentors to humanize the club and build trust with parents evaluating the program.
sections.headline: Meet the People Behind the Machines
sections.subheadline: Our coaches, mentors, and staff bring professional engineering experience and genuine enthusiasm to every session.

items.title: Dana Reyes — Club Director
items.description: Former aerospace engineer and FRC alumna. Dana founded BoltWorks after seeing too many talented kids without access to quality STEM programs.

items.title: Marcus Obi — Head Build Coach
items.description: Mechanical engineer with 10 years in robotics manufacturing. Marcus runs the fabrication floor and is famous for his 'no bad ideas' brainstorm sessions.

items.title: Priya Nair — Software Lead
items.description: Software developer and CS educator who designed BoltWorks' three-tier coding curriculum, from Scratch to ROS.

items.title: Tom Callahan — Outreach Coordinator
items.description: Former high school teacher turned STEM advocate. Tom manages school partnerships, scholarship programs, and community demo events.

pages.title: Departments
pages.goal: Give prospective members a clear, exciting map of every learning track and team division so they can identify where they belong and what skills they will gain.
pages.meta_description: Explore BoltWorks departments — from mechanical engineering and software to outreach and competition strategy. Find your track and start building.

sections.intent: Frame the departments page as a festival lineup — every department is a headliner with its own stage.
sections.headline: Every Builder Has a Home Here
sections.subheadline: BoltWorks is organized into specialized departments so every member can go deep on what they love most.
sections.body: Whether you're drawn to the precision of mechanical design, the logic of code, the strategy of competition, or the art of communicating science — there's a department built for you.

asset_ideas.subject: A set of six bold, festival-poster-style department icons: a gear (mechanical), a circuit chip (software), a trophy (competition), a megaphone (outreach), a wrench (fabrication), and a lightbulb (innovation lab)
asset_ideas.purpose: Visual identifiers for each department card in the grid, giving each track a distinct but cohesive visual identity

sections.intent: Present all six departments as equal, exciting options in a card grid so visitors can scan and self-select their path.
sections.headline: Six Tracks. One Team.
sections.subheadline: Each department runs its own projects, workshops, and competitions — all feeding into the same championship robot.

items.title: Mechanical Engineering
items.description: Design and build the physical systems of the robot — chassis, drivetrain, manipulators, and structural components. CAD, prototyping, and fabrication are core skills.

items.title: Software & Controls
items.description: Write the code that makes the robot move, sense, and decide. Students work in Python, Java, and C++ using real robotics frameworks like WPILib and ROS.

items.title: Electrical & Wiring
items.description: Design the power systems, wire the motors and sensors, and ensure the robot's electronics are safe, reliable, and competition-ready.

items.title: Competition Strategy
items.description: Analyze opponents, plan match strategies, scout other teams, and make real-time tactical decisions during tournament play.

items.title: Outreach & Communications
items.description: Tell the BoltWorks story to the world. Manage social media, write grant applications, organize community demos, and run our school ambassador program.

items.title: Innovation Lab
items.description: A free-build sandbox for members who want to pursue independent robotics projects, enter external hackathons, or prototype ideas beyond the competition robot.

sections.intent: Help prospective members and parents quickly compare age divisions and program formats to find the right fit.
sections.headline: Which Division Is Right for You?
sections.subheadline: BoltWorks runs three age-based divisions, each with its own competition league and curriculum depth.

items.title: Sparks Division (Ages 8–11)
items.description: Introduction to robotics through LEGO Mindstorms and VEX IQ. Focus is on fun, exploration, and learning the basics of sensors and programming. Competes in the Junior Robotics League.

items.title: Voltage Division (Ages 12–14)
items.description: Intermediate builders working with VEX EDR and custom electronics. Teams design full robots for regional VEX competitions and internal BoltWorks tournaments.

metadata.format: Two sessions per week + weekend builds

items.title: Apex Division (Ages 15–18)
items.description: The flagship program. Teams build full-scale competition robots for FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC). This is the most demanding and rewarding track BoltWorks offers.

metadata.format: Three sessions per week + intensive build season

items.title: Open Lab (All Ages)
items.description: Drop-in sessions for independent projects, skill workshops, and mentored free builds. No competition pressure — just making things.

pages.goal: Showcase BoltWorks' original student research projects and technical achievements to demonstrate depth, attract advanced students, and impress sponsors and partner institutions.
pages.meta_description: Discover BoltWorks student research projects — from autonomous navigation systems to AI-driven object detection. Real engineering, real results.

sections.intent: Frame the research page as a festival of ideas — a showcase stage for the club's most ambitious technical work.
sections.headline: Student Engineers. Real Research. Serious Results.
sections.subheadline: BoltWorks members don't just build competition robots — they push the boundaries of what young engineers can achieve.
sections.body: From autonomous navigation to computer vision and soft robotics, our research projects have been presented at regional science fairs, university symposia, and national STEM conferences. This is where curiosity becomes contribution.

asset_ideas.subject: A bold, festival-poster-style illustration of a robot arm reaching toward a glowing lightbulb surrounded by circuit traces and data graphs, evoking discovery and innovation

sections.intent: Present active and completed research projects as editorial cards so visitors can explore the breadth and depth of student work.
sections.headline: What We're Building Right Now
sections.subheadline: Each project is student-led, mentor-supported, and aimed at solving a real engineering challenge.

items.title: Project ARIA — Autonomous Robot Intelligence Architecture
items.description: A Voltage and Apex team collaboration developing a modular autonomous decision-making system using ROS2 and a custom sensor fusion pipeline. Goal: sub-3-second field mapping in FRC-scale environments.

items.title: SoftBot — Pneumatic Soft Robotics Gripper
items.description: An Innovation Lab project exploring soft robotic actuators made from silicone molds and pneumatic control. The team is testing grip reliability on irregular game pieces.

items.title: VisionTrack — Real-Time Object Detection for FRC
items.description: A software team project implementing a YOLOv8 model trained on competition game pieces to enable real-time targeting and autonomous scoring. Achieved 94% detection accuracy in field tests.

items.title: EcoBot — Sustainable Materials in Robot Construction
items.description: An outreach-driven research project investigating the use of recycled and bio-based materials in robot chassis design. Partnered with a local university materials science lab.

items.title: DriveMetrics — Drivetrain Performance Analytics Dashboard
items.description: A data engineering project that logs motor telemetry during practice matches and visualizes performance trends to guide mechanical tuning decisions.

sections.intent: Proactively answer the most common questions from parents and students to reduce friction and qualify leads before they contact the team.
sections.headline: Things People Usually Ask Us First

items.title: Does my child need prior experience to join?
items.description: Absolutely not. Most of our members start with zero robotics experience. Our Sparks and Voltage divisions are designed specifically for complete beginners.

items.title: What does membership cost?
items.description: Seasonal membership fees range from $150 to $350 depending on division. Need-based scholarships are available and cover up to 100% of fees. No student is turned away for financial reasons.

items.title: How do I enroll my child?
items.description: Submit an enrollment inquiry through the contact form above. Our team will schedule a free orientation session where your child can meet coaches and try a build activity before committing.

items.title: Can businesses or individuals sponsor BoltWorks?
items.description: Yes! Sponsorships start at $500 and include recognition on our competition robot, website, and event materials. Contact partners@boltworks.club for a sponsorship prospectus.

items.title: Do you partner with schools?
items.description: We have formal partnerships with six schools in the region and offer in-school demo programs and teacher training. Contact Tom Callahan at outreach@boltworks.club to explore a partnership.
